WORKSHEET · CLASS 27 · AGES 4 YEARS

Hedgehog’s Winding Path Worksheet for Age 4

A long winding road from hedgehog to strawberry — trace it, then try it smaller, then draw it yourself.

Download Worksheet ↓

Teaching tips
THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

The winding path is the marathon of pencil control: one long line that bends left and right without lifting. Tracing it slowly teaches your child that a wobble is not a stop — the pencil just carries on.

  • One continuous line, no lifting
  • Left-right eye tracking while drawing
  • Wrist and arm moving together
  • Finishing a long task with care

On the sheet: Trace the winding road from the green dot to the strawberry.

WHERE THIS FITS

The class behind it.

Busy Bee Loop Practice Worksheet for Age 4

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Loops are the pre-cursive gold standard: up, around, and into the next loop without lifting. Your child traces big loops first, then smaller ones, then draws a row — three sizes of the same skill.

  • Continuous loop movement
  • Even loop sizes
  • Top-to-bottom stroke direction
  • Confidence for later cursive

On the sheet: Trace the loop trail from the bee to the flowers, then draw your own loops.

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Waves train the hand to reverse direction smoothly at the top and bottom of each curve. Saying “up, down” aloud while tracing turns the sheet into a rhythm game, and rhythm is what makes handwriting fluent.

  • Smooth direction changes
  • Even wave height
  • Rhythm: saying the movement out loud
  • Row-by-row independence

On the sheet: Trace the three waves from the boat to the lighthouse.

Rocket Zigzag Mission Worksheet for Age 4

A sharp zigzag flight from rocket to planet — crisp corners are the mission.

Download Worksheet ↓

Teaching tips
THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as it prints.

This page is the worksheet’s home: see the whole sheet, download it or print it, and pass it on. Solving on screen happens in the class’s own activities on the Learning Path — this page is for the table, the kitchen and the fridge door.

ABOUT THIS WORKSHEET

What your child practices.

Zigzags are the first stop-and-turn stroke: the pencil must actually STOP at each corner and push off in a new direction. That stop-start control is exactly what letters like M, W and Z will demand.

  • Sharp corner turns
  • Stopping and restarting direction
  • Diagonal control
  • Mission persistence — it is a long line!

On the sheet: Trace the rocket’s zigzag path up to the planet.
